Problem Description

Troubleshooting
:
Thank you for performing the preliminary troubleshooting. Please review the steps outlined below. Additionally, please ensure to bring a spare fuse FC12 for the upcoming site intervention.
1. The fuse may blow due to various factors such as short circuits, overcurrent, component failure, and power surges.
2. Inspect the connections for any loose or short circuits in the power cables of KF10, BT1, and BT2, as FC12 directly connects to them.
3. Verify the FB2 breaker for a short circuit, as FB12 is for SMPS (TB17) converting AC to DC voltage, which could have caused the fuse to be damaged.
4. Check for the XD6, XD10 and XD41 terminal also for the short circuit . These terminal are connecting it to BT1 & BT2 temperature sensor.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0381441-DC/Si-D/QA-[MP / N5 160345957] FC12 flashing red CRM:00798001320
additional_info.body:
Hi Sadek,
Please try these 2 things.
FC14 tripping is an indicator for a short circuit (phase or ground)
FC14 is unfortunately a fuse for a lot of devices 🡪 complete door, cooling pump (depending on configuration, etc.), so if it is tripping the routers are off
Track it down to XD21 and more specifically to the display itself
At the displaycontroller there is a 3-pin connector for the 24 V
The same 24V are also routed through the board to a 10 pin connector for the RFID and credit card device
So there might be a short circuit somewhere in this chain 🡪 I would suggest to disconnect (all!) plugs of of RFID and CC in order to isolate the display
If FC14 is still stripping: the display controller or the connection from XD21 to the 3 pin controller is screwed up 🡪 metal sleeve falling of and short circuiting the board
Attached you can find more documents (Datasheet and wiring of the display, rework instruction for the display with a lot of detailed pictures.
Below are the steps followed on one of the chargers with the same issue. Please follow these as well:
Replace the FC14 → no result, so the problem was not hardware
Tighten the XD21 connections → worked momentarily, we could get the FC14 to green status but after a reboot, it went back to fault state.
Tightened the XD3 and XD8 connections → no result
Turn off FC14 and remove all the 24V connections to the XD21 except for pin 1.
Insert connection XD21:2 and turn ON FC14 again → green
Turn off FC14, and insert connection XD21:3 and turn ON FC14 → green
Repeat for all the connections and the connection XD21:4 (HMI 24 V) was the faulty one.
Visual inspection of the cables do not show any sort of damage.
Tried to move the connection from “under” FC14 to FC12 in connection XD3:4 to see if there is any fault in the circuit of FC14.
Also, we recommend carrying a spare HMI, if possible, to check if the HMI is found to be faulty.
If you need anything, just let us know.
Best Regards,
Sominath Nagalgaon
eMobility Support Team

additional_info.subject: ID0381441-DC/Si-D/QA-[MP / N5 160345957] FC12 flashing red CRM:00797001427
additional_info.body:
Dear Sadek,
I hope this message finds you well.
Based on the information you provided, it appears that the issue you are experiencing may be related to a short circuit, particularly with the HMI PCB. The symptoms you described, such as the fuse blowing after connecting the HMI, suggest that there could be a fault in the display controller or its connections.
We recommend trying a spare HMI to see if the HMI is faulty. This could help narrow down the issue. If needed, you can replace the HMI.
